newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech firm singled out for Zetor stake.
newsitem.headline: Czech firm singled out for Zetor stake.

text.p: Czech state-owned Konsolidacni Banka said on Tuesday it was in negotiations to sell a stake in the tractor maker Zetor a.s. to a domestic investor.
"We are negotiating with a Czech firm, but the details on the selection process we will not reveal because the process is continuing," spokeswoman Helena Zachystalova told Reuters.
The process should be completed by the end of the year, or the beginning of next year, she said. The size of the stake under consideration was not disclosed.
She said the bank had discussed the capital entry into the country's largest tractor maker with various foreign and Czech investors but discussions centre now on one domestic party.
Local media have reported that U.S. based John Deere & Co. and the Czech engineering conglomerate Skoda a.s. Plzen had been among the firms showing an interest in Zetor shares.

Konsolidacni, which specialises in recapitalising and restructuring Czech banks and industries, holds a 79.4 percent stake in the Brno-based Zetor following the privatisation of the company earlier in the decade.
Individual shareholders have 12.8 percent of Zetor, and investment funds hold 6.8 percent.
